subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should OpenClaw own Slack OAuth token rotation inside the bundled Slack plugin, and if so where should refresh tokens, client secrets, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens be stored and recovered?
rationale: The useful behavior is clear, but automation cannot safely choose the credential storage, redaction, migration, runtime adoption, and operator recovery model for rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Design plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Implement Slack rotation behind the Slack plugin boundary with secure storage, transactional refresh, status/doctor recovery, docs, and live Socket Mode plus HTTP Mode proof.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep OpenClaw on static Slack token inputs for now and document the operational workaround until maintainers want to own rotating Slack secrets.

options.title: Wait for a generic credential seam
options.body: First design a generic plugin credential-refresh contract, then implement Slack as one consumer of that contract.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Implement Slack rotation behind the Slack plugin boundary with secure storage, transactional refresh, status/doctor recovery, docs, and live Socket Mode plus HTTP Mode proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled Slack runtime/config history and is the best available owner for the security/product boundary choice.
